All standard due-diligence domains are uncovered: CAPEX vs. materials/equipment cost indices, contracted MW vs. executed interconnection/offtake agreements, schedule dates vs. permitting milestones, site control claims vs. title/lease evidence, and construction schedule vs. equipment lead times. rfis: Provide site address, APN, and proof of site control (purchase agreement, lease, or option) for the proposed project in Ventura County.
Provide zoning designation for the parcel and written confirmation from Ventura County Planning Division that solar+storage is a permitted or conditional use.
Provide preliminary title report and any recorded easements, liens, or encumbrances affecting the site.
Provide the interconnection application and queue position with Southern California Edison (SCE), including any study results (Feasibility, System Impact, Facilities Study).
Provide a copy of the executed interconnection agreement or, if not yet executed, the current status and timeline for completion.
Provide the executed power purchase agreement (PPA) or evidence of a merchant project, including offtaker creditworthiness and contract terms.
Provide the full financial model with CAPEX, OPEX, revenue, tax equity, and debt assumptions, including sensitivity analysis.
Provide equipment quotes and supply agreements for PV modules, inverters, transformers, and battery storage, including lead times and delivery schedules.
Provide the construction schedule with milestones for permitting, procurement, construction, and commercial operation date.
Provide evidence of tax credit eligibility (ITC/PTC) including beginning-of-construction documentation (e.g., notice to proceed, physical work, or 5% safe harbor).
Provide the CEQA status and any environmental assessments, including biological, cultural, and traffic studies.
Provide documentation of community outreach and any opposition or support from local stakeholders.
Provide evidence of compliance with California Fire Code and local fire department requirements for battery storage.
Provide any existing or planned interconnection upgrades and associated cost estimates from SCE.

agency_actions.action: Submit application for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) or verify that solar+storage is a permitted use under the current zoning ordinance.
agency_actions.why: Zoning prohibition is a kill-criterion; must confirm the project is allowed before further investment.
agency_actions.deadline: Submit within 30 days; approval typically 6–12 months.

agency_actions.action: Initiate interconnection study (Feasibility, System Impact, Facilities Study) and obtain a cost estimate and timeline for interconnection agreement.
agency_actions.why: Interconnection is a critical path item; without a viable interconnection, the project cannot proceed.
agency_actions.deadline: Initiate within 30 days; studies may take 6–18 months depending on queue position.

agency_actions.action: Verify that the interconnection process and any PPA tariff comply with CPUC rules, and confirm if a CPUC approval is required for the offtake agreement.
agency_actions.why: Regulatory compliance is necessary to avoid delays or rejection of the PPA.
agency_actions.deadline: Review within 60 days; approval may take 3–6 months if required.

agency_actions.action: Determine if the project exceeds 50 MW and requires a CEC license; if so, initiate the application process.
agency_actions.why: Projects >50 MW must obtain CEC certification; failure to do so is a legal barrier.
agency_actions.deadline: Determine applicability within 30 days; licensing can take 12–24 months if required.

agency_actions.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW)
agency_actions.action: Conduct a preliminary environmental review to identify any sensitive species or habitats on the site and initiate consultation if needed.
agency_actions.why: CEQA compliance may require mitigation for biological resources; early engagement reduces risk of delays.
agency_actions.deadline: Initiate within 60 days; consultation may take 3–6 months.

agency_actions.agency: Ventura County Air Pollution Control District (VCAPCD)
agency_actions.action: Verify if construction or operation requires an air quality permit (e.g., for diesel generators or dust control).
agency_actions.why: Air quality permits are often overlooked and can cause construction delays.
agency_actions.deadline: Assess within 30 days; permit issuance typically 2–4 months.

verification_requests: Verify SCE interconnection queue position and study results directly with SCE, including any required network upgrades and cost allocation.
Verify offtaker creditworthiness and contract terms (e.g., PPA price, duration, termination clauses) through financial statements and credit reports.
Verify equipment lead times from suppliers (PV modules, inverters, transformers, battery systems) against the construction schedule; obtain written confirmation of lead times.
Verify tax credit eligibility documentation (beginning-of-construction evidence) with tax counsel to ensure compliance with IRS rules.
Verify site control and title by obtaining a title commitment and reviewing lease/purchase agreement for assignability and termination clauses.
Verify CEQA status with Ventura County Planning Division to confirm whether an exemption applies or an EIR is required.
Verify any community opposition or support through public records and stakeholder interviews.
conditions_precedent: Zoning confirmed to allow solar+storage (permitted or conditional use) with no unresolved prohibition.
Site control secured via executed purchase agreement or lease with clear title and no fatal encumbrances.
Interconnection agreement executed or at least a completed System Impact Study with no fatal constraints and acceptable upgrade costs.
Offtake agreement executed (or merchant project validated with market analysis) with creditworthy counterparty.
Tax credit eligibility established with documented beginning-of-construction evidence (ITC/PTC).
Equipment procurement contracts in place with lead times compatible with the construction schedule.
CEQA compliance achieved (exemption confirmed or EIR certified) with no unresolved environmental issues.
Financial model validated against benchmark CAPEX ($1.43–1.56/Wac) and revenue projections, with sensitivity analysis showing acceptable returns.
All required permits (CUP, building, electrical, fire) identified and application submitted or obtained.
Community opposition assessed and mitigation plan in place if needed.
